claims.text: Visit frequency has fallen 6% year on year while basket size is stable, so the problem is how often people come, not what they buy.
Price and peak-time queues appear to be the main reasons lapsed customers shop elsewhere.
Personalised offers look promising: early receipt-coupon tests suggest redemption is several times higher than generic coupons.
Evidence suggests testing personalised offers through receipts before committing to an app, since 60+ shoppers (46% of revenue) lean towards printed offers.
Hypothesis to test: a loyalty app would lift visit frequency. Survey interest conflicts with weak engagement in the existing scheme.
App-based coupons need POS middleware costing £150–220k, likely over half the digital budget.

conflicts.description: Stated app interest (58%) conflicts with low engagement in the existing loyalty scheme (14% redeemed).
conflicts.how_to_resolve: Fake-door test of app sign-up in 2 stores measuring actual sign-ups.

conflicts.description: Lapsed customers cite price and queues; the commercial director believes the lack of an app is the cause.
conflicts.how_to_resolve: Larger lapsed-customer survey with ranked reasons.

gaps.missing: Whether queue reduction would lift visits
gaps.why_it_matters: Queues may be a cheaper fix than an app
gaps.would_raise_confidence: Staffing trial at peak in 2 stores tracking visit frequency
